key_insight: PhysForge decouples functional reasoning from geometry synthesis to generate 3D assets that are physically grounded and interaction-ready, using a large PhysDB of 150,000 assets with four-tier physical annotations.
problem_solved: Existing 3D asset generation focuses on static geometry and ignores functional and physical properties needed for realistic interaction in virtual worlds and embodied AI. PhysForge addresses the gap by producing assets with explicit functional logic and hierarchical physics attributes.
method: Decoupled two-stage pipeline: (1) predict functional logic + hierarchical physics descriptors, (2) synthesize geometry and physical parameters conditioned on those descriptors.
Train and validate using PhysDB — a large-scale dataset of ~150,000 assets annotated with four tiers of physical/functional information to ensure assets behave plausibly in simulation.
Design the system to enforce consistency between affordances, material/rigidity properties, and simulated dynamics for interactive use.
impact: Enables scalable creation of interaction-ready 3D assets for simulation, games, and embodied AI, reducing manual engineering and improving realism of physics-driven behaviors for downstream training and evaluation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: two-stage decoupled workflow (functional reasoning → geometry + physics synthesis).
Dataset infographic: 150k assets and four-tier annotation breakdown (affordance, material, kinematics, dynamics).
Before/after comparison: conventional static-model vs PhysForge physics-grounded asset in a simple interaction (e.g., opening, stacking, collision).
Hierarchy chart: visualization of the four-tier physics annotations and how they feed into synthesis.
paper_title: PhysForge: Generating Physics-Grounded 3D Assets for Interactive Virtual World
paper_authors: Yunhan Yang, Chunshi Wang, Junliang Ye, Yang Li, Zanxin Chen
